title: Risk management and insurance
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Identify and measure market, credit, liquidity, operational and model risk; compute value at risk and expected shortfall; stress-test portfolios; understand bank capital rules; and explain insurance principles, products and enterprise risk management.

weeks.1: Risk and the risk management process
weeks.3: Value at risk: parametric, historical and Monte Carlo
weeks.9: Bank capital and the Basel framework

blocks.deliverable: Classify the risks of three businesses.
Compute VaR three ways for one portfolio.
Compute expected loss for a loan book.
Week 7 midterm; design a stress test.
Explain one risk failure and its lessons.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Risk report: for a given portfolio or institution, measure its market and credit risk, compute VaR and expected shortfall, run three stress scenarios in Python, and write a three-page risk report with recommendations.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
